_doc: The weekly scout report: what exists out there that this box is not using. Written by the Claude routine described in docs/models.md and read by src/lib/model-scout.ts. Judgment lives here; facts about which model ids a vendor currently sells are NOT — those are pulled live from each vendor's model-list endpoint at read time, because a list committed to git is out of date the day after it is written. Fit verdicts are likewise computed at read time against the live machine, never stored here: a verdict depends on what is running and how much disk is free, and both change hourly.
_schema: candidates[]: { id, name, kind: local|cloud, capability, why, checkpoint?, provider?, target?, mode?, params?, released?, license?, docs?, paper?, requirement? { vramGb, ramGb, diskGb, basis, estimated }, spec? { paramsB, precision, contextK, kind }, pricing? }. Give `requirement` when the authors published usable numbers; give `spec` otherwise and let estimateFromParams() do the arithmetic with an honest basis string. upgrades[]: { alias, from, to, why } — a like-for-like repoint of an alias already in ai-router.yaml.
generatedBy: weekly scout, 2026-09-14 — the image lane closed. Z-Image-Turbo and FLUX.2-klein-4B, carried here for three and two weeks, were installed and measured on 12 September, so both leave candidates by adoption rather than by being beaten. That empties this report of image work and leaves it entirely audio: the one new entry is tencent/AuK, an MIT speech foundation model that went public on 9 September and took the top of the TTS trending board from the `license:other` model this report has been holding out on for a month.

candidates.name: Qwen3-ASR 1.7B (transformers build)

requirement.basis: Disk EXACT from the repo listing, re-read this week and byte-for-byte unchanged: model.safetensors 4,076,193,080 B plus tokenizer and config = 4,087,646,324 B for the whole repo. That file size divided by the 2,038,052,480 params HF reports is exactly 2 bytes/param, so the release is bf16 and there is no hidden encoder or codec outside the count — unlike the TTS entries below. VRAM is 4.09 x 1.15 runtime overhead, not measured; host RAM is the server process only, since a model this size stays resident on the card.

candidates.why: Still the drop-in replacement for local-whisper on the path that already exists, and still the first thing to install if only one audio model gets added. whisper large-v3 shipped November 2023 and is the oldest checkpoint on this box; Qwen3-ASR is Apache-2.0, current, and its repo enumerates 30 languages in metadata (zh, en, yue, ar, de, fr, es, pt, id, it, ko, ru, th, vi, ja, tr, hi, ms, nl, sv, da, fi, pl, cs, fil, fa, el, hu, mk, ro). It costs 4.7 GB against whisper's measured 1.5 GB, which is rounding error on a 32 GB card — and against the 14-16 GB the three newly-installed image models each measured on 12 September, it is the cheapest upgrade left on this list. The `-hf` repo rather than the base one because the base ships custom code and cannot be served through the OpenAI audio API the way local-whisper is wired; the base repo has ten times the downloads (2.77M against 281K) and is the wrong one for this box.

candidates.name: VibeVoice-ASR-Streaming 1.5B
candidates.params: 2.81B (the '1.5B' in the name is the LLM backbone only)

requirement.basis: Disk EXACT from the repo listing, re-read this week and unchanged: model-0000{1,2,3}-of-00003.safetensors 2,498,354,152 + 2,486,576,066 + 643,458,072 B = 5.63 GB of weights, 5,645,212,528 B for the whole repo. Against the 2,814,116,321 params HF reports that is exactly 2 bytes/param, so it is a bf16 release with no separate codec outside the count. Note the name understates it: '1.5B' is the language backbone, the checkpoint is 2.81B. VRAM is 5.63 x 1.15 runtime overhead, not measured; host RAM is the server process only. The 7B sibling is 17.36 GB (8,674,021,857 params, same 2 bytes/param) and is the more popular of the two on the hub this week — trending 95 against the 1.5B's 22 — but on this card it runs alone and blocks every image model, so the 1.5B is the one to run here.

candidates.why: Unchanged from last week and still the only clean-licensed way to get live transcription onto this card. It does two things neither whisper nor any Apache alternative can: it streams speaker-attributed transcription — who said what, as the audio arrives — and it takes user-supplied hotwords for names and jargon. local-whisper transcribes finished audio, so the console can never show live text from it, and it does not diarise at all; that is a zero, not a smaller number. The cost is 5.63 GB against whisper's measured 1.5 GB, which buys 9 extra languages (en, zh, es, pt, de, ja, ko, fr, ru, it) plus diarisation on a card that now has room for it. Plain MIT from Microsoft Research, which is why it beat NVIDIA's nemotron-3.5 here despite that model being smaller and covering 35 languages — see notes. Twelve days old with a demo space and a technical report; verify WER against whisper before repointing anything. It is a NEW service, where Qwen3-ASR above is a repoint of one that already works — install that first.

candidates.name: Qwen3-TTS 12Hz (1.7B CustomVoice)

requirement.basis: Disk EXACT from the repo listing, re-read this week and unchanged: model.safetensors 3,833,402,552 B (= 1,916,676,352 params x 2 bytes, so bf16) PLUS speech_tokenizer/model.safetensors 682,293,092 B, which the 1.7B in the name does not include — 4,520,218,951 B for the whole repo. VRAM is that x 1.15 runtime overhead. Not measured. Ignore the repo's `usedStorage` of 4,604,822,661 B; it counts revisions the download does not fetch.

candidates.why: The cheap, proven half of the TTS answer, and the one to install if only one goes in. local-kokoro is 82M and sounds like it; Qwen3-TTS-12Hz is Apache-2.0, expressive, controllable, supports custom voices, and at 2.62M downloads and 1,964 likes is the most-pulled clean-licensed TTS on the hub by an order of magnitude. Its real footprint is 4.52 GB rather than the 3.83 GB the parameter count implies, because of the separate speech tokenizer. It survives this week specifically against AuK below, which is better at more things and 1.5x the size: this entry is the drop-in for the :8002 service that already speaks the OpenAI audio_speech API, where AuK is an instruction-driven pipeline and therefore a new service to write. Cheapest first. Its one real weakness against the field is that its repo declares no languages at all, where the Apache near-miss VoxCPM2 declares 30 for 0.44 GB more — see notes.

candidates.name: AuK (Tencent Hunyuan speech foundation model)
candidates.params: authors say 1.5B; the repo ships 6.76 GB, so the count is not the footprint

requirement.basis: Disk EXACT from the repo listing: auk_base.safetensors 6,122,209,092 B + vae.safetensors 637,322,604 B = 6.76 GB, 6,762,657,404 B for the whole repo. HF publishes NO parameter count for this repo — the safetensors index carries no dtype summary — so there is no per-param arithmetic to check the file size against, and estimateFromParams() must not be used on it: the card calls AuK '1.5B', which against 6.76 GB of weights would be 4.5 bytes/param, so the name is describing one component and not the checkpoint. VRAM is 6.76 x 1.15 runtime overhead, not measured. Host RAM is the server process only: at 6.76 GB the weight set fits on the card outright, so unlike the image models this needs no CPU offload and holds no standing host-RAM cost. AuK-Flash, the 4-step distilled sibling, is byte-for-byte the same size (auk_flash.safetensors 6,122,209,092 B + the same VAE) — pick between them on latency, not memory.

candidates.why: New this week, and it settles the TTS licence question the same way VibeVoice settled the streaming-ASR one. For a month the best trending TTS model was BreezeBlue/Breeze-TTS-2, held out here because it is `license:other`; AuK is plain MIT from Tencent Hunyuan and has taken the top of the board outright — trending 194 against Breeze's 73, which itself fell from 237 last week. Against local-kokoro it is not a better reader of text, it is a different class of tool: one instruction interface doing zero-shot voice cloning, content and acoustic and paralinguistic editing of existing recordings, speech enhancement, and source separation. Kokoro scores zero on all four, and so does everything else on this box — nothing here can clean up a noisy recording or split two speakers apart. The cost against the Qwen3-TTS entry above is +2.24 GB (6.76 vs 4.52) and a new service rather than a repoint of :8002. The honest caveat is age and evidence: the weights went public on 9 September and the repo has 1,202 downloads, so this is a five-day-old model recommended on its licence, its authorship and its capability list, not on adoption. The base repo declares no languages and AuK-Flash declares only zh and en — check that your text is covered before writing the service.

upgrades.why: Raised last week, still unactioned, and still the most urgent of the five because the current target is being retired rather than merely superseded: gpt-5.5 is no longer carried in OpenAI's published pricing table while the 5.6 line is, and ai-router.yaml still points the hand-written `gpt-5.5` alias at it. OpenAI positions gpt-5.6-terra as 'performance competitive with GPT-5.5' at a lower price — $2/$12 per 1M input/output tokens against gpt-5.5's $5/$30 as recorded when this repoint was first raised on 2026-09-07, so the like-for-like swap is also a 2.5x cost cut on both sides of the meter. Terra, not sol or luna: sol is the flagship and luna the cheap tier, so both change what the alias means, and this alias is the stable one applications call. This is exactly the repoint docs/models.md says the console cannot make for you — familyKey() strips version tokens and cannot see that 'terra' is a tier name, so gpt-5.5 -> gpt-5.6-terra never gets the `supersedes` label. All three 5.6 ids are already wired under their own names from the 2026-08-19 wire-all; only the alias is stale. Re-check the prices against the live discovery join before editing — this report did not call the vendor this week.

Unchanged and now four weeks outstanding. claude-opus-5 shipped 2026-07-24 and claude-opus-4-8 on 2026-05-28 — two generations on, same tier, same alias. The wire-all on 2026-08-19 added a separate `claude-opus-5` alias, so the model is already reachable and already paid for; the stable hand-written `claude-opus` alias that applications call is the only thing still pointing at 4-8. Repointing it is a one-line edit to ai-router.yaml (line 82) that nothing in the console will do for you.

Unchanged and now four weeks outstanding. claude-sonnet-5 shipped 2026-06-29; the wired claude-sonnet-4-6 dates from 2026-02-17, which makes this the most stale alias in the file at nearly seven months. As with claude-opus, a parallel `claude-sonnet-5` alias already exists from wire-all, so the repoint costs nothing but the edit at line 68.

Unchanged and now four weeks outstanding. gemini-3.7-flash is live on the v1beta ListModels endpoint and already wired under its own id from the wire-all, but the stable `gemini-flash` alias at line 61 still points at 3.6. Google publishes no release dates, so this is a version-number judgement rather than a dated one — but the flash line moves fast and the wired alias is one behind. Do NOT repoint it at gemini-flash-latest, which is also wired: see the note about pinning below.

Unchanged and now four weeks outstanding. gpt-transcribe appeared 2026-07-27, dropping the 4o generation marker the way gpt-image did; gpt-4o-transcribe dates from 2025-03. It is wired under its own id already, but the `openai-transcribe` alias at line 108 still fronts the 4o model. Note gpt-live-transcribe shipped the same day for streaming, which the router's audio_transcription mode does not front — the VibeVoice candidate above is the local answer to that gap, and this repoint is the cloud half of the same problem.

notes: ADOPTED, and the reason this report is shorter: on 12 September this box installed Z-Image-Turbo (NVFP4) and FLUX.2-klein-4B, which had been the top two entries here for three and two weeks, plus HiDream-O1 Dev FP8, which this report never listed. All three are in config/model-meta.json now and all three RAN — docs/image-model-experiment-2026-09-12.md records 1024x1024 in 6.2-7.3 s for Klein at 16,390 MiB whole-card, 10.2-14.2 s for Z-Image at 14,074 MiB, and native 2048x2048 in 13.3-18.3 s for HiDream at 15,653 MiB, all measured with nvidia-smi at 500 ms intervals. They leave candidates by adoption, not by being beaten, and the image lane now has no open candidate at all: nothing in this week's text-to-image trending list is both clean-licensed and smaller than what is already installed.

THE FOLLOW-ON NOBODY HAS DONE YET, and the single cheapest win on this box: local-flux-schnell and local-qwen-image are now dead weight. Both were REJECTED by admission control during the 12 September experiment — schnell on its ~28 GB RAM / ~31.7 GB VRAM profile, Qwen-Image on its 28 GB RAM estimate against 28.94 GB available — while the three new models did the same job at 14-16 GB whole-card. That is the arithmetic this report has been making the case for since Z-Image first appeared here, now confirmed on the actual card. Their weights are still on D: (schnell's stack alone is 31.81 GiB: flux1-schnell 22.15, t5xxl_fp16 9.12, clip_l 0.23, ae 0.31), and removing them frees more disk than every candidate on this list combined needs to download. This is a decision for a human, not a scout — schnell is the only model here anyone has A/B'd against for two years — but it should be a deliberate keep rather than an accident.

THE PATTERN WORTH REMEMBERING, and the reason this report exists beside the Leaderboard tab: for anything that is not a plain LLM, the parameter count is not the footprint, and the gap is usually a text encoder or a codec sitting outside the count. This week's example is the new one: AuK's own model card says '1.5B' and the repo ships 6.76 GB, which would be 4.5 bytes/param — and HF publishes no parameter count for it at all, so estimateFromParams() has nothing correct to work from. The back catalogue: LLaDA-Image is '6.54B' and ships 49.2 GB. FLUX.2-klein-4B is '3.88B' and ships 23.7 GB, half of it a Qwen3 text encoder. Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B carries a 0.68 GB speech tokenizer the name omits. VibeVoice-ASR-Streaming-1.5B is really 2.81B. Every requirement in this report is built from the repo's actual file byte counts; do not let a parameter count size one of these when the file listing is one API call away. Two of the models on this box now have MEASURED whole-card figures instead, which is better still.

THIS WEEK'S LEADERBOARD TRAP, and it is a text one: Edge0/Edge0-35B-A3B-preview is the #2 trending model on the entire hub (score 1191, 1,223 likes in six days), Apache-2.0, and 19.74 GB on disk — which is to say the Leaderboard tab will size a 34.66B MoE at 4-bit, find it fits this card with room to spare, and be completely wrong. It is `library:mlx`: Apple-silicon only, and tagged `ssd-offload` and `prerouter` besides, because it is a LoRA-plus-router rig over Qwen3.6-35B-A3B built for unified-memory edge devices. It will not run on an RTX 5090 at any quantisation. The base model it adapts is the thing to look at here, and that one the Leaderboard already ranks correctly. (For contrast, the #1 trending model overall, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, is MIT and 763B params shipping 510 GB even at mixed fp8/int8 — the Leaderboard refuses that one correctly and needs no help from this report.)

Held out on licence, ASR: oruk/orukeet (9 Sep) is the most interesting thing this report is NOT recommending. It covers 25 European languages, ships ready-to-serve GGUF, .nemo and sherpa-onnx int8 builds, and the q8 GGUF is 714,456,704 B — half the size of the whisper large-v3 int8 build currently serving :8001, which would make it the first ASR upgrade here that COSTS less than the incumbent rather than more. It is `license:cc-by-sa-4.0`. That is a real open licence rather than a bespoke one, but share-alike on model weights raises a question about derivatives and possibly outputs that nobody here has answered, and it is v0.1.0 at five days old. Per docs/models.md it stays in notes until a human reads the terms. nvidia/nemotron-3.5-asr-streaming-0.6b remains `license:other` (the NVIDIA Open Model License) and is still the best-on-merit streaming model by coverage — 638M params and 35 languages against VibeVoice's 2.81B and 10 — but VibeVoice adds speaker attribution and hotwords under plain MIT, so the licence read is only worth doing if those 25 extra languages matter to you specifically.

TTS alternatives seen and not adopted. openbmb/VoxCPM2 remains the standing near-miss and got no worse this week: Apache-2.0, 2.29B, 4,960,731,866 B from its file listing, 384K downloads, voice cloning and voice design across 30 DECLARED languages — where Qwen3-TTS's repo declares none at all. It is held out only because it is 0.44 GB larger than Qwen3-TTS for the same job; if multilingual TTS is the actual need rather than English and Chinese, swap the two and take the 0.44 GB. Held out on licence: BreezeBlue/Breeze-TTS-2 (3.47B, 7.68 GB, `other`, and this week overtaken by AuK — trending 73 against 194); bosonai/higgs-tts-3-4b (4.65B, 9.32 GB, `other`, but 100 declared languages, which is far and away the widest coverage in open TTS and the reason to read that licence if coverage is the constraint); fishaudio/s2-pro; Supertone/supertonic-3; darkps/ice-012-audio (cc-by-nc). k2-fsa/OmniVoice (600+ languages, 1.2M downloads) still publishes no licence tag at all, so it stays out entirely. Edge0/Audio8-TTS-Preview-0.6b has gone quiet and no longer justifies a line.

Image models still blocked on licence, and one of them is now blocked on size too: krea/Krea-2-Turbo remains GATED and `license:other`, and reading its file listing this week settles the question anyway — 12.82B params, 61,995,040,979 B on disk, bf16 with an F32 component. Even past the gate it needs a quantised community build to run here at all, so the ecosystem argument for clicking through the gate is much weaker than it looked. Also still `other`: Gazingstars123/Anima-2.9B, briaai/Fibo-1.5 (gated), ideogram-ai/ideogram-4-nf4, lodestones/Kroma. inclusionAI/LLaDA-Image and LLaDA-Image-Turbo-FP8 remain the Apache-2.0 unified generate-and-edit models that do not fit: 49.24 GB bf16 and 27.58 GB fp8, because the '6.5B' counts only the transformer and the llada2uni MoE text encoder is five times its size. With Klein now installed and measured at 16,390 MiB doing the same generate-plus-edit job, LLaDA is comprehensively beaten here and not worth watching further.

Both wired Gemini image models still report the 429 quota error recorded in model-meta.json. That is a billing state on the key, not a model choice — no scouting will fix it. Separately, gemini-pro stays pinned to gemini-3.1-pro-preview on purpose: Google publishes gemini-pro-latest as a moving alias and ai-router.yaml pins explicit versions so an archived result records which model actually produced it. Both -latest aliases are wired under their own names from the wire-all, which is fine; do not repoint a stable alias at one.

Text LLMs are deliberately absent from candidates. The Leaderboard tab ranks every open-weights text model with a published parameter count against this card automatically, and cloud discovery carries live prices — a hand-written candidate there would go stale beside data that does not. This report's only two contributions in the text lane are the gpt-5.5 upgrade above, which discovery cannot make because OpenAI's tier names look like ordinary words to familyKey(), and the Edge0 note above, which is the opposite case: a model the automatic ranking will happily say fits when it cannot run here at all.
